name: What is the difference between a second-story addition and a pop-top addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a second-story addition and a pop-top addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A second-story addition generally refers to adding new square footage above a portion of the existing ground floor footprint, often extending the original roofline. A 'pop-top' addition is a specific type where the entire existing roof is removed, and a new full second story is built on top of the original structure. The choice often depends on existing architectural style, budget, and desired outcome, with pop-tops potentially offering more cohesive new living space. Hometelligent Inc. can guide clients in Berkeley and other service areas on which approach best suits their property.
acceptedAnswer.description: A second-story addition adds space above part of the home, while a pop-top replaces the entire roof with a new full second story.
